2.6 "P2 Incident" means a partial loss of service or a significant degradation in performance affecting a subset of transactions or a single client, where service is not fully interrupted.

2.7 "P3 Incident" means a minor issue that does not materially impact service availability, such as cosmetic defects, documentation errors, or non-critical functional bugs.

2.8 "Resolution" means the point at which the underlying cause of an Incident has been identified and a workaround or permanent fix has been applied such that the service is restored to normal operation.

2.9 "Working Day" means any Calendar Day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in India.

---

3. SERVICE COMMITMENTS

3.1 Availability Commitment

The GPI production service shall be available 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, measured across all covered services. Availability is calculated as:

(Available Minutes – Downtime Minutes) / Available Minutes × 100

Downtime is measured from the time RELOPS acknowledges an Incident until the time Resolution is achieved. Scheduled maintenance windows, as notified to clients at least 72 hours in advance, are excluded from downtime calculations.

3.2 Incident Response Targets

RELOPS shall respond to Incidents according to the priority classification assigned at the time of reporting. Response time is measured from the moment the Incident is logged in the RELOPS tracking system, regardless of the channel used to report it.

3.3 The SLA document states that the Service Level Agreement has_sla_response_time of 15 minutes. Record status: current. This commitment applies to P1 Incidents only and is effective from the date of this version of the agreement.

3.4 Resolution targets are measured from the time of logging to the time of Resolution. If a workaround is provided that restores service to normal operation, the Incident is considered resolved for the purpose of this SLA, even if a permanent fix is deferred.

3.5 For P1 Incidents, if Resolution is not achieved within the target time, the Incident shall be escalated to the RELOPS Incident Manager, who shall invoke the Major Incident Management process and engage additional resources as required.

---

4. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1 RELOPS (Reliability Operations) is the primary point of contact for all Incidents and service requests related to GPI. RELOPS operates on a 24x7 basis and can be reached through the channels listed in Section 7.

4.2 Clients are responsible for providing accurate and complete information when reporting an Incident, including the affected transaction IDs, timestamps, and any error messages observed. Incomplete information may delay diagnosis and shall not be counted against RELOPS response targets.

4.3 Clients are expected to notify RELOPS of planned changes to their integration, such as certificate rotations or API version upgrades, at least 5 Working Days in advance. This notice period allows RELOPS to prepare support and avoid unintended service disruption.

4.5 The GPI Service Manager, appointed by RELOPS, shall be the single point of accountability for service quality and shall participate in quarterly service reviews with clients.

---

5. EXCLUSIONS

5.1 This SLA does not apply to failures caused by:
- Client-side infrastructure, network, or application issues
- Force majeure events, including but not limited to natural disasters, acts of government, or widespread telecommunications outages
- Scheduled maintenance windows notified in advance
- Unauthorised access or malicious actions by third parties not attributable to RELOPS negligence
- Use of the service in a manner not consistent with published documentation

5.2 Downtime during a scheduled maintenance window shall not be counted toward availability calculations, provided that clients were notified at least 72 hours in advance.
- Personal data processed through GPI is handled in accordance with the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
- Cross-border data transfers are supported through approved mechanisms, including standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules where applicable.
- Data retention periods follow the published GPI Data Retention Schedule. Clients may request deletion of their data after the contractual retention period ends.

6.4 Security controls and assurances:

- Access to GPI production systems is restricted to authorised personnel and enforced through role-based access control (RBAC) with multi-factor authentication (MFA).
- All administrative access is logged and monitored. Logs are retained for a minimum of 180 days and are reviewed periodically by the Security Operations team.
- Encryption is applied in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256) for all GPI data.
- Vulnerability assessments are conducted quarterly, and penetration tests are performed at least annually by an independent third-party assessor.
- RELOPS maintains a formal incident response plan aligned with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) framework. Clients will be notified of any security incident affecting their data within 24 hours of confirmation.

6.5 Audit and review schedule:

- Annual external audits for ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and PCI DSS.
- Quarterly internal audits covering access reviews, change management, and backup restoration testing.
- Client audits may be conducted with 30 days written notice, subject to confidentiality obligations and reasonable scheduling constraints. Audit reports and findings will be shared with the client on a confidential basis.

6.6 RELOPS shall provide a summary of compliance posture during the quarterly service review, including any material findings from audits or assessments conducted in the preceding quarter.

8. SERVICE REVIEW AND REPORTING

8.1 RELOPS shall provide monthly performance reports covering availability, incident response times, resolution times, and any SLA breaches. Reports shall be delivered by the 5th Working Day of the following month.

8.2 Quarterly service reviews shall be conducted with each client to review performance trends, discuss upcoming changes, and address any outstanding issues. The GPI Service Manager shall chair these reviews.

8.3 Annual compliance reviews shall be conducted no later than 30 days before each certification expiry date to confirm renewal status and communicate any changes to clients.

---

9. TERM AND TERMINATION

9.1 This SLA shall be effective from the date of signing and shall remain in effect until terminated by either party with 90 days written notice.

9.2 Upon termination, RELOPS shall provide a transition period of 60 days to facilitate orderly migration of services. Data export in a mutually agreed format shall be provided at no additional cost during this period.

9.3 Sections 6 (Compliance and Certifications) and 8 (Service Review and Reporting) shall survive termination for a period of 12 months.
10. CHANGE MANAGEMENT

10.1 Any change to the Services, the Service Levels, or the underlying infrastructure that may materially affect the delivery of the Services shall be subject to the Change Management Process described in this Section 10.

10.2 RELOPS shall maintain a Change Advisory Board (the "CAB") comprising representatives from RELOPS engineering, operations, and service management functions. The GPI Service Manager shall act as the chair of the CAB.

10.3 Clients may nominate one representative to attend CAB meetings as an observer. Such observers shall receive CAB meeting invitations and minutes but shall not have voting rights.

10.4 Proposed changes shall be classified as follows:

| Change Category | Definition | Approval Authority |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | Pre-approved, low-risk, routine changes (e.g., patching, minor config updates) | RELOPS Shift Lead |
| Normal | Changes with moderate risk or potential client impact | CAB (via majority vote) |
| Emergency | Changes required to prevent or mitigate a major incident or security vulnerability | GPI Service Manager (with post-change CAB review within 5 Working Days) |

10.5 The change request shall include, at minimum: a description of the change, the reason for the change, the proposed implementation window, a risk assessment, a rollback plan, and a list of affected services and clients.

10.6 RELOPS shall provide at least 10 Working Days' advance notice for Normal changes that may cause a degradation of Service Levels. Emergency changes shall be communicated as soon as reasonably practicable, and in any event no later than 24 hours after implementation.

10.7 Scheduled maintenance windows are defined in Schedule B. Time spent in a scheduled maintenance window shall be excluded from the calculation of Availability, provided that RELOPS has given the required advance notice.

---

11. SERVICE CREDITS

11.1 If RELOPS fails to meet a Service Level in any calendar month, the Client shall be eligible for a Service Credit as set forth in the table below. Service Credits shall be calculated based on the Monthly Recurring Charges ("MRC") for the affected Service.

| Service Level | Measurement Period | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| Availability < 99.9% but ≥ 99.5% | Calendar month | 5% of MRC |
| Availability < 99.5% but ≥ 99.0% | Calendar month | 10% of MRC |
| Availability < 99.0% | Calendar month | 20% of MRC |
| Incident Response Time missed | Per incident | 2% of MRC (max 10% per month) |
| Incident Resolution Time missed | Per incident | 2% of MRC (max 10% per month) |

11.2 Service Credits shall be applied as a deduction against the next monthly invoice. The total Service Credits in any calendar month shall not exceed 30% of the MRC for that month.

11.3 To claim a Service Credit, the Client shall submit a written request to the GPI Service Manager within 30 days of the end of the month in which the Service Level was missed. RELOPS shall validate the claim against the monthly performance report and confirm the credit within 15 Working Days.

11.4 Service Credits shall be the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet a Service Level, except as otherwise provided in the Master Services Agreement.

---

12. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

12.1 In addition to the monthly performance reports described in Section 8.1, RELOPS shall provide the following reports:

| Report | Frequency | Delivery Deadline | Content |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekly Incident Summary | Weekly | Each Monday | List of incidents, severity, status, and preliminary root cause |

2.6 "P2 Incident" means a partial loss of service or a significant degradation in performance affecting a subset of transactions or a single client, where service is not fully interrupted.

2.7 "P3 Incident" means a minor issue that does not materially impact service availability, such as cosmetic defects, documentation errors, or non-critical functional bugs.

2.8 "Resolution" means the point at which the underlying cause of an Incident has been identified and a workaround or permanent fix has been applied such that the service is restored to normal operation.

2.9 "Working Day" means any Calendar Day that is not a Saturday, Sunday, or public holiday in India.

---

3. SERVICE COMMITMENTS

3.1 Availability Commitment

The GPI production service shall be available 99.9% of the time in each calendar month, measured across all covered services. Availability is calculated as:

(Available Minutes – Downtime Minutes) / Available Minutes × 100

Downtime is measured from the time RELOPS acknowledges an Incident until the time Resolution is achieved. Scheduled maintenance windows, as notified to clients at least 72 hours in advance, are excluded from downtime calculations.

3.2 Incident Response Targets

RELOPS shall respond to Incidents according to the priority classification assigned at the time of reporting. Response time is measured from the moment the Incident is logged in the RELOPS tracking system, regardless of the channel used to report it.

3.3 The SLA document states that the Service Level Agreement has_sla_response_time of 15 minutes. Record status: current. This commitment applies to P1 Incidents only and is effective from the date of this version of the agreement.

3.4 Resolution targets are measured from the time of logging to the time of Resolution. If a workaround is provided that restores service to normal operation, the Incident is considered resolved for the purpose of this SLA, even if a permanent fix is deferred.

3.5 For P1 Incidents, if Resolution is not achieved within the target time, the Incident shall be escalated to the RELOPS Incident Manager, who shall invoke the Major Incident Management process and engage additional resources as required.

---

4. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

4.1 RELOPS (Reliability Operations) is the primary point of contact for all Incidents and service requests related to GPI. RELOPS operates on a 24x7 basis and can be reached through the channels listed in Section 7.

4.2 Clients are responsible for providing accurate and complete information when reporting an Incident, including the affected transaction IDs, timestamps, and any error messages observed. Incomplete information may delay diagnosis and shall not be counted against RELOPS response targets.

4.3 Clients are expected to notify RELOPS of planned changes to their integration, such as certificate rotations or API version upgrades, at least 5 Working Days in advance. This notice period allows RELOPS to prepare support and avoid unintended service disruption.

4.5 The GPI Service Manager, appointed by RELOPS, shall be the single point of accountability for service quality and shall participate in quarterly service reviews with clients.

---

5. EXCLUSIONS

5.1 This SLA does not apply to failures caused by:
- Client-side infrastructure, network, or application issues
- Force majeure events, including but not limited to natural disasters, acts of government, or widespread telecommunications outages
- Scheduled maintenance windows notified in advance
- Unauthorised access or malicious actions by third parties not attributable to RELOPS negligence
- Use of the service in a manner not consistent with published documentation

5.2 Downtime during a scheduled maintenance window shall not be counted toward availability calculations, provided that clients were notified at least 72 hours in advance.

- Personal data processed through GPI is handled in accordance with the Information Technology (Reasonable Security Practices and Procedures and Sensitive Personal Data or Information) Rules, 2011 under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
- Cross-border data transfers are supported through approved mechanisms, including standard contractual clauses and binding corporate rules where applicable.
- Data retention periods follow the published GPI Data Retention Schedule. Clients may request deletion of their data after the contractual retention period ends.

6.4 Security controls and assurances:

- Access to GPI production systems is restricted to authorised personnel and enforced through role-based access control (RBAC) with multi-factor authentication (MFA).
- All administrative access is logged and monitored. Logs are retained for a minimum of 180 days and are reviewed periodically by the Security Operations team.
- Encryption is applied in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (AES-256) for all GPI data.
- Vulnerability assessments are conducted quarterly, and penetration tests are performed at least annually by an independent third-party assessor.
- RELOPS maintains a formal incident response plan aligned with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) framework. Clients will be notified of any security incident affecting their data within 24 hours of confirmation.

6.5 Audit and review schedule:

- Annual external audits for ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, and PCI DSS.
- Quarterly internal audits covering access reviews, change management, and backup restoration testing.
- Client audits may be conducted with 30 days written notice, subject to confidentiality obligations and reasonable scheduling constraints. Audit reports and findings will be shared with the client on a confidential basis.

6.6 RELOPS shall provide a summary of compliance posture during the quarterly service review, including any material findings from audits or assessments conducted in the preceding quarter.

9. TERM AND TERMINATION
